title: Humidity, Pollen, and Duct Film: A Vienna Homeowner Guide
headline: Maple Avenue colonials, Wolf Trap oaks, and why finished basements sweat at the trunks
description: The Town of Vienna sits under a heavy Fairfax County canopy. An educational look at why 1950s–70s colonials store pollen in cool basement trunks, and when to clean the ducts from Burke.

sections.heading: Vienna looks walkable. The pollen load is a forest.
paragraphs: Maple Avenue, Church Street, and Glyndon Park do not look like woods until April. Then every car on Chain Bridge Road is yellow. Oak and maple from the Wolf Trap canopy dump pollen onto decks, then onto returns. A 1950s–70s colonial with a full basement stores that load in the coolest metal in the house — the supply trunks.
Those trunks get cold when the AC runs. Indoor air in July is wet. Condensation forms. Dust sticks. That is the film you wipe off a Nutley Street register on Monday and see again by the weekend.

sections.heading: Rec-room additions hide the joints that collect dust
paragraphs: A Vienna colonial that gained a rec room in the 1990s often has original trunks plus a later branch. Dust settles at those splices. Vienna/Fairfax-GMU Metro and the Tysons edge add denser townhomes with dryer runs that turn too many times before the cap. The same humidity that fogs a windshield on Maple Avenue in July is sitting on the air handler.
If wiping the registers only lasts a few days, when you are ready to book, use the [Vienna, VA location page](/locations/vienna).

sections.heading: Typical signs in a Vienna house
listItems: Yellow-gray film on upstairs supplies during peak pollen.
Musty air from a finished basement when the AC starts after rain.
A dryer that needs two cycles in a Tysons-edge or Metro-area townhome.

Keep basement humidity under 50% in summer.
Clean ducts every 3 to 5 years; clear dryer vents about once a year.

faq.q: Do humid summers alone require duct cleaning?
faq.a: Humidity helps dust stick and can support growth on cold coils, but cleaning decisions still depend on inspection and history.
